status: exploratory; frozen before any site is coded
author: asi-jerusalem worker, regional round 9 October 2026
purpose: Code the Archaeological Survey of Israel (ASI) site records near the project's places: features, periods and distances. No identification claim.
exposure_before_freeze: Service_Eng.aspx/GetMapNameAndId, GetFilteredMaps (first page), GetMaps: the list of 153 online maps with ids, numbers, authors, centre points
GetIsraelGrid.aspx: map sheet rectangles (first two features printed)
Service_Eng.aspx/GetSites?mapId=63: site names and numbers of Map 102 (a keyword list of names was printed)
Service_Eng.aspx/GetSiteDesc2?Id=13785: the full English record of Map 102 site 486 ('En Rogel)
Service_Eng.aspx/GetPolygonsSites?MapId=63: the first three GeoJSON features (Map 102 sites 1-3) were printed
Earlier repository notes (registration/entry40_*.md) used GetSiteDesc2 for Map 83/1 sites near Beth Horon
places_rule: Every row of places_v2.csv with numeric lat and lon is placeable. Rows without coordinates (jer_shaveh, transjordan) are listed as not placeable and get no distance or look row.

source.host: https://survey.iaa.org.il/ (robots.txt returns 404, so no rule forbids these paths)

endpoints.sheets: aspxService/GetIsraelGrid.aspx (GeoJSON rectangles; properties.itemid = map id, properties.name = map number)

source.request_rules: HTTP GET with header Content-Type: application/json, at most one request per second, every response cached once in the scratch folder with its SHA-256; no images, plans or map scans are fetched.
source.remains_probe: GetSiteRemains is called for the first 10 selected sites of each map (by site number). If all 10 are empty, the other sites of that map are not queried. Non-empty remains are coded with the same rules as extra text of their site.

map_selection: Select every online map whose sheet rectangle lies at most 3 km (haversine to the nearest point of the rectangle) from at least one placeable place. A map with no sheet rectangle is not selected.
site_selection: From each selected map's English GeoJSON, keep sites whose GeoJSON point lies within 3.5 km of any placeable place; fetch their English record (GetSiteDesc2). Final membership uses the primary coordinate: a site enters sites.csv if it lies within 3.000 km of at least one placeable place.

coordinates.primary: The record's 'New Israel Grid' value. Read the larger number as the northing and the smaller as the easting (in Israel ITM northings exceed 350000 and eastings are below 300000). Convert EPSG:2039 (Israel 1993 / Israeli TM Grid) to EPSG:4326 with pyproj Transformer.from_crs('EPSG:2039','EPSG:4326', always_xy=True), as W2B scripts/grid_convert.py does for the old grid.
coordinates.fallback_1: If the grid value is missing or unparsable, use the record's 'WGS-84' field (lat, lon) and set coord_method = source_wgs84.
coordinates.fallback_2: If both are missing, use the GeoJSON point and set coord_method = geojson_point.
coordinates.check: Report the distance in metres between the converted grid point and the record's WGS-84 field. Flag coord_check = 'gt50m' when it exceeds 50 m.
coordinates.nearest_place: Nearest placeable place by haversine; ties broken by place_id in alphabetical order. sites.csv also lists every place within 1 km and within 3 km.

text_fields: Classification text = English site name + 'Additional Names' + 'Finds' field of GetSiteDesc2 + the English description + the GeoJSON finding text + any remains text. Bibliography, map name, map number, survey type, field number and grid values are excluded.

feature_classes.note: Regular expressions, Python re, case-insensitive. One features.csv row per (site, class) when the class matches anywhere in the classification text. Class names follow the project's landmark classes (T02 entry_features LEX2CLASS) where one exists; the others are survey-only classes.

hebrew_check.note: Applied to the Hebrew GeoJSON description and finding text of the same site id. A class found in Hebrew but not in English is listed in sites.csv heb_only_classes. It does not create a features.csv row.

periods.matching: Labels are matched case-insensitively, longest alternative first, without overlap. The verbatim matched text is kept as period_as_given.
periods.precedence: Before matching, the alternatives of all three lists are sorted by the length of the pattern string, longest first, so 'Early Roman' wins over 'Roman' and 'Early Hellenistic' over 'Hellenistic'.
periods.site_level: site_finds_in_window (sites.csv): 'yes' if any 'within' label occurs in the site's English text fields; else 'overlaps' if any 'overlaps' label occurs; else 'no' if any 'outside' label occurs; else 'unknown'. This is context for the site, not a feature date.
periods.feature_level: A feature's date = the period labels in the same sentence of the English description as the class match (sentences split at '. ', '! ', '? ' or end of text). dated_in_window: 'yes' if every attached label is 'within'; 'partly' if at least one attached label is 'within' or 'overlaps' and not all are 'within'; 'no' if all attached labels are 'outside'; 'unknown' if no label is attached (including matches found only in the name or Finds field). Site pottery never dates a feature.

quotes.rule: At most 12 whitespace-separated words, verbatim after HTML tags and entities are removed and whitespace is collapsed. features.csv: the 12-word window of the source field that contains the first class match, starting up to 4 words before it. sites.csv: the first 12 words of the English description.

citation: '{Author}, ASI Map of {map name} ({map number}), site {site number}; survey.iaa.org.il record {site id}; printed page not given online'. The online record is unpaginated; the site number is the locator inside the printed volume. If the map introduction names the printed volume and year, the README states it.
protected_zone: No ASI image is opened. Any site within 1 km of tell_es_sultan is flagged protected_zone_nearby = yes; its text may be coded, but the README must say so and it is not usable as unseen evidence for the strip just north of Tell es-Sultan.
coverage_statements: Each selected map's introduction (English and Hebrew) is read for statements of what area was or was not surveyed and how. A look's coverage is filled only when the introduction states it for the place's area: 1.0 if it states full survey of that area, 0.0 if it states the area was excluded; otherwise null with an UNKNOWN basis. p_recognise, p_report and p_survive stay null unless a source states them.

looks.schema: Exactly the columns of research/models/search_effectiveness/looks.csv, same order.
looks.rows: One row per (candidate pair in candidates_v2.csv, lookable landmark class of that entry in entry_features.csv) where the place is placeable and its 1 km circle intersects at least one selected map sheet.
looks.not_lookable: valley, corner, threshold, rock, stone, field, court, chamber, fissure, pillar, outlet, upper_storey and any other class: a survey record cannot show or exclude them as coded here.
looks.result_rule: reported if at least one ASI site within 1.000 km of the place point has a features.csv row in a crosswalk class; otherwise silent. explicit_absence is never coded (a survey list does not state absence).
looks.satisfies_requirement: unknown for reported rows (no identification is attempted); empty for silent rows.
looks.ids: ASI-L001 upward, sorted by entry order in entries_v2.csv, then place_id, then landmark class.
looks.lineage: One lineage per ASI map survey (the field survey behind that map).

tests: unittest in tests/: plan hash equals the README value; CSV schemas; every quote has at most 12 words; two builds from the cache give byte-identical outputs.
